title: _save_csv opens in 'w' mode, silently discarding prior ablation rows on a narrower re-run
description: run_ablation.py writes results with _save_csv opening the output CSV in write ('w') mode, so re-running with a narrower --datasets/--models/--seeds selection overwrites and discards all previously computed ablation rows instead of merging. This is the inverse of the append-without-dedup hazard elsewhere: here legitimate prior results are silently lost. (Added by the completeness-critic pass. run_ablation.py is otherwise the one script that seeds correctly with [42,123,456], measures real spike metrics via SpikeRecorder/measure_spike_metrics, and has a __main__ guard - it wires to the legacy bi-modal package, not M7.)
evidence: _save_csv opens the CSV in 'w' (overwrite) mode at ~461-470; no merge with existing rows keyed by (dataset,model,seed)
fix: Merge new rows with any existing CSV keyed by (dataset,model,seed) before writing (upsert), or append then drop_duplicates on that key; do not blindly overwrite.
